models._description: Adds the 'totp_mail' email-OTP MFA branch (_mfa_type/_mfa_url/_check_credentials), the code generator/sender, the 2FA invite, and new-connection security alerts
On unlink, email the owning user a 'trusted device removed' security alert
Settings toggle that maps to ir.config_parameter 'auth_totp.policy' (enforce 2FA for employees / all users)

routes.note: Not a new route - controllers/home.Home extends auth_totp's Home.web_totp (@http.route() re-decoration keeps path '/web/login/totp', type='http', auth='public', methods GET/POST). The override fires AFTER super() to send the email OTP.

security.note: No own ACL/groups/record rules. It reuses auth_totp's security and base groups: the 2FA invite server action (data/ir_action_data.xml) is restricted to base.group_erp_manager, and the 'activate 2FA' link action to base.group_user. All OTP send/check runs sudo() during the pre-authentication (pre_uid) phase. uses_api_keys=true is inherited from auth_totp (totp_mail also forces _rpc_api_keys_only).

views.note: 2 res.users form inherits (an 'Invite to use 2FA' button on the security form; a stripped 'Enable 2FA' form reached from the invite mail) + a res.config.settings view for the enforce toggle + a QWeb inherit of auth_totp.auth_totp_form adding the email-code instructions and a 'Re-send email' POST button. No new model, so no list/search.

behavioral_notes.observation: This is the join point into auth_totp's login gate. When the pre-auth controller posts a code with credentials['type']=='totp_mail', _check_credentials (res_users.py:137) first calls _totp_rate_limit('code_check') (auth_totp caps it at 5/hour), derives the key with _get_totp_mail_key, and verifies with TOTP(key).match(token, window=3600, timestep=3600). CRUCIALLY there is NO per-user stored secret like authenticator-app TOTP: _get_totp_mail_key returns hmac(env(su=True), 'auth_totp_mail-code', (self.id, self.login, self.login_date)).encode() - a deterministic HMAC bound to the user id + login + last login_date, so a password change/new login rotates the key automatically. The 3600s window/timestep means the same 6-digit code is valid for ~1 hour (matching the email-delivery use case) instead of the 30s authenticator window. On success it purges BOTH the code_check and send_email rate-limit counters and returns the auth dict {uid, auth_method:'totp_mail', mfa:'default'}; on miss it raises AccessDenied('Verification failed, please double-check the 6-digit code'). Entirely invisible to ORM metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: res.users._mfa_type / _mfa_url / _rpc_api_keys_only (policy-driven email-2FA enrolment without a device)
behavioral_notes.observation: _mfa_type (res_users.py:115) extends auth_totp: if super() returns None (user has NO authenticator-app TOTP), it reads ir.config_parameter 'auth_totp.policy' and returns 'totp_mail' when policy=='all_required', or 'employee_required' AND self._is_internal(). So email-OTP is the FALLBACK second factor that the admin can force on users who never set up an app - they get a one-time emailed code instead. _mfa_url then returns '/web/login/totp' for the totp_mail type (reusing auth_totp's controller + form). _rpc_api_keys_only returns True for totp_mail too, so a policy-enforced user cannot use password RPC. This wires email-2FA into auth_totp's existing _mfa_type/_mfa_url extension points with no new route or device record.

The GET (or re-POST) of the TOTP form triggers the email. controllers/home.Home.web_totp (controllers/home.py) calls super() (auth_totp's render), then - only if response is 200 and the user's _mfa_type()=='totp_mail' and the session is still pre_uid (not yet uid) - opens a cr.savepoint() and calls user._send_totp_mail_code(); any AccessDenied/UserError (e.g. rate limit hit) is shown as the form error instead of crashing. _send_totp_mail_code (res_users.py:180) rate-limits via _totp_rate_limit('send_email') (5/hour), requires an email (else UserError), and sends mail.template 'auth_totp_mail.mail_template_totp_mail_code' force_send with email_layout 'mail.mail_notification_light', injecting request context (location via GeoIP city/country, device, browser, IP) so the email warns about the new-device login. The template calls object._get_totp_mail_code() at render time, which computes hotp(key, counter) with counter=int(timestamp/3600) and zero-pads to 6 digits, returning (code, human expiration '~1 hour'). The 'Re-send email' button in the inherited form simply re-POSTs the route to re-render and re-send (still rate-limited).

Beyond login, the module nudges users to set up REAL app-based 2FA. action_totp_invite (res_users.py:92), bound to a base.group_erp_manager server action on res.users list/kanban (data/ir_action_data.xml), filters recipients to users with no totp_secret and send_mails the 'auth_totp_mail.mail_template_totp_invite' template (force_send, light layout), then returns a display_notification toaster listing invited users. get_totp_invite_url returns '/odoo/action-auth_totp_mail.action_activate_two_factor_authentication'; clicking it runs a base.group_user server action that calls action_open_my_account_settings to open a stripped, non-editable res.users form (auth_totp_mail.res_users_view_form) showing only the 'Enable 2FA' button. So email here serves two distinct jobs: deliver a login OTP, and deliver an enrolment invitation.

behavioral_notes.element: res.users security alerts + auth_totp.device.unlink notification (mail.thread security-update emails)
behavioral_notes.observation: The module turns several account events into emails via _notify_security_setting_update (from auth_signup/base): res.users.write fires '2FA Activated'/'2FA Deactivated' alerts when totp_secret is set/cleared; authenticate() -> _notify_security_new_connection emails 'New Connection to your Account' ONLY when the user has _mfa_type() set and the request's td_id cookie does NOT match a trusted auth_totp.device (i.e. a genuinely new device); and the auth_totp.device.unlink override emails 'Security Update: Device Removed' (listing device names, grouped per user via _classify_by_user) when a trusted device is revoked. _notify_security_setting_update_prepare_values also injects suggest_2fa = (flag and not totp_enabled) so the security-alert template only nags users who haven't enabled app-2FA. These cross-model email side-effects are pure behaviour, absent from metadata.

frontend_gap3 present=false: 0 JS modules, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 services, 0 patches. The only client-side artifact is static/tests/totp_flow.js (a browser test), so the only asset bundle touched is web.assets_tests (1). The entire UX is server-rendered: QWeb inherits of the auth_totp login form (email-code text + 'Re-send email' button), res.users/res.config.settings backend form inherits, and emailed mail.templates. No custom OWL component is shipped.

it_architecture.application: auth_totp_mail (email-delivered one-time-code second factor + 2FA invitation/enforcement layered on auth_totp's login flow)
software_services: /web/login/totp (public HTTP, inherited from auth_totp; override emails the OTP on render)
logical_data_erm: totp_mail OTP key = hmac(self.id, self.login, self.login_date) — derived, no stored secret table
information_flows: depends: auth_totp (login MFA gate, rate-limit, TOTP/hotp), mail (mail.template send_mail)
challenge: web login -> _mfa_type()=='totp_mail' -> _mfa_url='/web/login/totp' -> web_totp GET -> _send_totp_mail_code -> email OTP
verify: web_totp POST -> _check_credentials(type='totp_mail') -> TOTP(_get_totp_mail_key()).match(token, window=3600) -> session.finalize | AccessDenied
invite: erp_manager server action -> action_totp_invite -> mail_template_totp_invite -> get_totp_invite_url -> action_open_my_account_settings (Enable 2FA form)
alerts: write(totp_secret) / authenticate() new-device / device.unlink -> _notify_security_setting_update emails

capabilities: Email-delivered one-time-code second factor (fallback when no authenticator app)
Policy-based 2FA enforcement (employees-only / all users) via settings
Security-event email alerts (2FA on/off, new-device login, trusted-device removed)
Reuse of auth_totp rate-limiting on both code send and code check
value_streams: Login-by-Email-OTP: password accepted -> held at pre_uid -> _mfa_type='totp_mail' -> code emailed -> user enters code -> _check_credentials -> session finalized
Enforce-then-Onboard: admin sets auth_totp.policy + sends invite -> user opens Enable-2FA form -> sets up app-based TOTP (graduates off email OTP)
information_concepts: res.users (the authenticating identity; no new field, behaviour only)
totp_mail OTP (derived HMAC code, ~1h validity, not persisted)
organization: base.group_user (receives invite link / opens Enable-2FA form)
policies: Enforcement policy: ir.config_parameter 'auth_totp.policy' in {employee_required, all_required} drives _mfa_type fallback to totp_mail
Rate limits (inherited from auth_totp): 5 emailed codes/hour (send_email) and 5 verifications/hour (code_check) per user, AccessDenied on breach, purged on success
Code validity: ~1 hour (window=timestep=3600) vs the 30s authenticator window
Key rotation: OTP key bound to (id, login, login_date) so it self-rotates on login/credential change
Invite targets only users without totp_secret; nag/suggest_2fa suppressed once app-2FA is enabled
stakeholders: End user / employee (receives and enters the emailed login code; may be invited to set up app-2FA)
Security administrator / ERP manager (enforces 2FA policy, sends invites)
Mail subsystem (delivers the OTP and invite/alert emails)
auth_totp base module (owns the login gate, rate-limit ledger and TOTP/hotp crypto this module reuses)
metrics: auth.totp.rate.limit.log rows for send_email / code_check (abuse / delivery-retry signal, owned by auth_totp)
count of users covered by policy (auth_totp.policy) vs users with app-based totp_secret

classification.rationale: auth_totp_mail is IT security infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It owns NO business object - 0 own models, only behaviour grafted onto res.users / auth_totp.device / res.config.settings - and exists solely to add an email-delivered one-time-code second factor (and policy enforcement + invitations) to the login that every module sits behind (auto_install=true, depends auth_totp + mail). It creates no document chain and holds no customer/order/product/ledger data, so it is 'support', not chain/shop/network. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the precise fit: this is the 'manage IT security / identity & access management' capability - the concrete running access-control mechanism (email OTP generation/verification, MFA challenge wiring, rate-limited delivery, enforcement policy). It mirrors its parent auth_totp (also 8.0/support). 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation and Resiliency' was considered (2FA mitigates account-takeover risk and supports compliance), but rejected: 11.0 is the governance layer (risk registers, control frameworks, audits), whereas auth_totp_mail is the technical *implementation* IT builds and operates. The numbering 8.0 = 'Manage Information Technology' matches the name.

standard_capabilities: Email one-time-code as a second factor when a user has no authenticator app
Code wired into auth_totp's existing login gate (_mfa_type='totp_mail', _mfa_url='/web/login/totp', _check_credentials)
Derived (non-stored) HMAC code keyed to user id+login+login_date, ~1h validity (window=3600)
Rate limiting on both emailed codes and verifications (5/hr each, inherited) with new-device context (GeoIP/IP/browser) in the email
Policy enforcement via Settings: require 2FA for employees only or all users (ir.config_parameter auth_totp.policy)
Admin 2FA invitation email + one-click Enable-2FA onboarding form
Security-event alert emails (2FA activated/deactivated, new-device login, trusted-device removed)
typical_fits: Forcing 2FA org-wide even for users who never installed an authenticator app (they get email codes)
Onboarding users onto app-based 2FA via the 'Invite to use 2FA' bulk action
Notifying users of suspicious new-device logins and device revocations by email
Tightening login security without deploying SMS/hardware tokens
common_gaps: Email OTP is weaker than app-based TOTP (email-account compromise defeats it) - intended as a fallback/bridge, not the recommended factor
Delivery depends on the mail subsystem (outgoing mail server + the user's reachable email); no SMS/push channel here
~1h code validity is much longer than a 30s authenticator code (larger interception window)
Enforcement is a coarse two-level policy (employees / all); no per-group or risk-based rules out of the box
No self-service backup-codes / recovery flow beyond admin disable (inherited from auth_totp)
drive_hints: odoo shell: u=env['res.users'].browse(2); u._mfa_type()  # 'totp_mail' once auth_totp.policy is set and user has no app-2FA
odoo shell: env['res.users'].sudo().browse(2)._send_totp_mail_code()  # rate-limited send (needs an email)
curl -i 'http://localhost:8069/web/login/totp'  # without a pre_uid session -> redirect to /web/login (the gate)

open_questions: Exact interplay with auth_totp's _assert_can_auth login-attempt budget and how it composes with the send_email/code_check 5/hr limits during a flaky-email retry storm.
Whether deployments actually set auth_totp.policy (enforcement) in practice and the resulting email-OTP vs app-TOTP adoption mix - needs runtime data (models empty at capture).

Behaviour when the same emailed code is replayed within the 1h window - unlike app-TOTP's totp_last_counter replay guard, the email path relies on the hour-long match window and rate limits rather than a per-code one-time-use counter.
